experiences.name: Eagle Bay Brewing Co
experiences.description: A family-owned brewpub on the family's working farm at Eagle Bay, brewing preservative-free beers on site and serving seasonal plates with views over Cape Naturaliste farmland to the Indian Ocean. Two estate vineyards supply the house Eagle Bay wines, and the whole operation runs on solar power and rainwater.

image.alt: The Eagle Bay Brewing Co farm lawn and brewpub under a big marri at golden hour
image.verified: their own venue photo (eaglebaybrewing.com.au) served via Wayback Machine snapshot 2025-11-08 because their Cloudflare blocks hotlinking; downloaded 2026-07-11 and visually verified: farm lawn, brewpub and marri at sunset

briefing.icebreaker: Everything here runs on the family farm: the beer is brewed metres away, the wine comes off their own two vineyards, and the power comes off the roof.
briefing.proMove: Order a tasting paddle and a wood-fired feed, then claim the lawn; kitchen hours finish before the bar, so eat first.
briefing.hiddenGem: The Sugarloaf Rock and Cape Naturaliste lighthouse lookouts are minutes away, making this the natural lunch stop on a cape loop.

experiences.sommNote: Even a Cabernet loyalist needs a palate reset, and there is no finer place for one than this lawn with the ocean on the horizon.

experiences.name: Wild Hop Brewing Company
experiences.description: A big timber taproom in the Yallingup bushland on Wildwood Road, pouring small-batch beers brewed on site, with chesterfield lounges inside and lawns and gardens running into the trees. Open seven days, with a full kitchen and a steady rotation of limited releases on the taps.

image.alt: Inside the Wild Hop taproom: tasting paddles, leather chesterfields and garden beyond
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-11, viewed and verified: taproom interior with paddles and chesterfields, ambient people

briefing.icebreaker: This is the newest of the cape's bush breweries, and the tap list changes fast enough that the locals check it like a surf report.
briefing.proMove: Take the tasting paddle before you commit to pints, and grab the chesterfields by the glass wall if they are free.
briefing.hiddenGem: Wildwood Road is the quiet back way between Yallingup and Dunsborough, so you can pair it with Windows Estate or Happs without touching Caves Road traffic.

experiences.sommNote: The tasting paddle here is what Semillon palates call a sorbet course: bright, cold and rude not to.

experiences.name: CBCo Brewing Margaret River
experiences.description: The brewery formerly known as Colonial, founded on this Osmington Road site in 2004 and renamed CBCo in 2020. A big family-friendly farm venue just outside Margaret River town with a beer garden under sail shades, a playground on the lawn, a food-truck kitchen and the full core range brewed in WA on the taps.

image.alt: The CBCo beer garden from the bar rail, sail shades over the lawn and playground
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-11, viewed and verified: beer garden from bar rail, people ambient from behind

briefing.icebreaker: This is where the whole story started in 2004, when it was Colonial Brewing; the name changed in 2020 but the brewhouse never moved.
briefing.proMove: Saturdays run an hour later than the rest of the week; order the paddle and let the kids at the playground while you work through it.
briefing.hiddenGem: The venue sits on Osmington Road farmland five minutes from town, so it pairs neatly with a McHenry Hohnen or Xanadu afternoon.

experiences.sommNote: Twenty years of brewing history in a paddock; the lager at the end of a tasting day is practically a regional tradition.

experiences.name: Margaret River Brewhouse
experiences.description: The town's own brewery, opened in January 2016 by three local families among the karri trees on Bussell Highway, an easy walk from the main street. Beers are brewed on site under the Margaret River Beer Co label, the kitchen runs all day, and the garden fills with locals and their dogs by mid-afternoon.

image.alt: The Brewhouse table from above: share plates, beers and the timber deck
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-11, viewed and verified: overhead table spread of food and beers, no faces

briefing.icebreaker: Three local families opened this in 2016 so the town would have a brewery it could walk to, and it still feels exactly like that.
briefing.proMove: It is open to 9pm seven days, the latest of the region's breweries, so save it for after the cellar doors shut at five.
briefing.hiddenGem: The karri-shaded garden is barely five minutes on foot from the main street, making it the rare brewery you can reach without a designated driver.

experiences.sommNote: When the last cellar door closes at five, the town walks here; join it and argue about the day's best Cabernet over a pale ale.

experiences.name: Rocky Ridge Busselton Taphouse
experiences.description: The original taphouse of Rocky Ridge, the decorated farm brewery from nearby Jindong, a stone's throw from the Busselton foreshore on Marine Terrace. A wall of more than twenty taps runs the full spectrum from crisp farm lagers to imperial stouts, with the tap boards changing weekly.

image.alt: The tap wall and boards at Rocky Ridge Busselton Taphouse
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-11, viewed and verified: bar with 20+ taps and menu boards, ambient people

briefing.icebreaker: Rocky Ridge brews on a working family farm out at Jindong and is one of Australia's most sustainability-decorated breweries.
briefing.proMove: The tap wall runs past twenty lines and rotates weekly; ask what is fresh off the farm and order thirds to cover more ground.
briefing.hiddenGem: They hold the lease on the legendary Bootleg Brewery site at Wilyabrup, currently in renovation, so watch this space for the region's next big reopening.

experiences.sommNote: A jetty-side pit stop between the capes and the vines; the farm lager travels from Jindong faster than most wines travel to their own cellar doors.

experiences.name: Shelter Brewing Co
experiences.description: A soaring concrete-and-glass brewhouse right on the Busselton foreshore, next to the famous jetty, brewing on site and serving from 7am coffee and bagels through to 10pm last drinks, seven days. The great hall's window wall opens to the lawn, and the ocean is close enough to read the swell from your stool.

image.alt: The main hall at Shelter Brewing Co with its giant window to the foreshore
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-11, viewed and verified: concrete great hall interior with window wall to the foreshore

briefing.icebreaker: The brewery sits so close to the Busselton Jetty that you can time your beer to the train trundling out along its two kilometres.
briefing.proMove: It opens at 7am for coffee and bagels, so it doubles as the breakfast stop before you drive down to the capes.
briefing.hiddenGem: The lawn side of the great hall catches the sunset over Geographe Bay, and the kitchen runs later than almost anywhere between here and the river mouth.

experiences.sommNote: Jetty, swell, sunset, lager: the correct order of operations before a Margaret River week begins in earnest.
